finding.claim: StartActionByGet and StartActionByGetAndWait start actions without enforcing the justification requirement, so actions configured to require a justification run with an empty one that is stored in the audit log.
finding.source: Any caller who passes UserFromApiCall and has exec permission on the action (or guest, if allowed). Request needs only actionId; no justification field is read.
finding.sink: executor.ExecRequest -> execution plus audit log entry with empty Justification (protected operation: justification-required control).

trace.note: StartActionByGet builds the request with no justification read or validation.
ExecutionRequest constructed with Arguments only; Justification field omitted.
ExecRequest called directly; no validateJustificationRequired call on this path.
StartActionByGetAndWait has the same gap: no validateJustificationRequired call (contrast StartActionAndWait at 308-311).
runBindingAndWait builds ExecutionRequest with no Justification, then ExecRequest at 354.
stepRequestActionPopulateLogEntry sets entry.Justification = ResolveJustification(req).
ResolveJustification: empty provided justification -> defaultJustificationForRequest.
defaultJustificationForRequest returns systemJustificationDefaults[username], which is empty for normal users. No error is returned; the executor never rejects an empty justification.
Enforced on the StartAction path (161 calls validateJustificationRequired, api_justification.go:18-24). Missing on the GET paths.

finding.guards_checked: Checked validateJustificationRequired (api_justification.go:18-24) and its callers: only StartAction (api.go:161), StartActionAndWait (api.go:309), and RestartAction via validateRestartLogEntry (api_log_arguments.go:49-51) enforce it. The executor does not reject empty justifications. Required-argument RejectNull checks still apply, so the bypass reaches only actions with no required arguments (or with defaults). Exec ACL is enforced in stepACLCheck (executor.go:831-845), so the caller still needs exec permission.

finding.claim: The client-supplied 'provider' header is trusted unconditionally. Sending provider: system with a username header makes the caller a 'system' execution, which skips the justification requirement.
finding.source: HTTP request header 'provider' (client-controlled), together with the username header configured as AuthHttpHeaderUsername. Reachable directly, or through a proxy that does not strip the 'provider' header.
finding.sink: validateJustificationRequired bypass (api_justification.go:30-31) via executor.IsSystemExecution (justification.go:26-32). Protected operation: justification requirement on StartAction and StartActionAndWait.

trace.note: Username taken from the configured header when AuthHttpHeaderUsername is set.
Provider taken from the raw 'provider' request header with no allowlist, no trusted-proxy check, and no tie to the username header.
runAuthChain returns the header user because Username is non-empty; checkUserFromHeaders runs first in authChain (line 15).
StartAction calls UserFromApiCall, which yields the header user with Provider 'system'.
validateJustificationRequired is called with that user.
justificationProvided returns true when IsSystemExecution(user) is true, even with an empty justification.
IsSystemExecution: Provider == 'system' and Username != 'guest' -> true.

finding.guards_checked: Username != 'guest' is the only check in IsSystemExecution. The caller must still hold exec ACL for the action. The bypass depends on the operator enabling trusted-header auth (AuthHttpHeaderUsername) and on the 'provider' header reaching OliveTin. Whether the reverse proxy strips it was not verifiable from this code. Impact is limited to skipping the justification requirement (and the empty justification being recorded), not ACL escalation.

finding.claim: The OAuth2 state value is also the logged-in session identifier (cookie olivetin-sid-oauth). It is logged at Info on login start (:185) and at Error on callback failures (:205, :217). Anyone with log access can replay it as the cookie and act as the victim. The OAuth authorization code is also logged at Debug (:311).
finding.source: Any reader of the server logs (log files, log shipping such as Datadog/Sentry, or debug output). Precondition: a victim has started an OAuth login and completed the callback.
finding.sink: Session authentication: CheckUserFromOAuth2Cookie -> lookupOAuth2UserByState returns the victim's username and usergroup (protected operation: session authentication).

trace.note: HandleOAuthLogin stores registeredStates[state] for the new login.
setOAuthCallbackCookie sets olivetin-sid-oauth = state (HttpOnly, but the value is the session ID).
log.Infof writes the state in plaintext at Info level, unconditionally.
HandleOAuthCallback sets Username and Usergroup on registeredStates[state] after the code exchange.
CheckUserFromOAuth2Cookie reads cookie olivetin-sid-oauth; the attacker sets it to the logged state.
lookupOAuth2UserByState returns the victim identity (Provider 'oauth2') with no IP/UA binding.
Error log 'State mismatch: %v != %v' prints both the query state and the cookie state.
Debug log prints the OAuth authorization 'token-code'.
Same pattern for local sessions: Warn logs the 'sid' cookie value on a stale session.

finding.guards_checked: Cookie is HttpOnly, Lax, and secure when TLS is in use, which only protects against script access, not log access. Server-side expiry is not enforced at lookup (lookupOAuth2UserByState 409-424 does not check createdAt). sweepExpiredOAuthStatesLocked (142-149) runs only from HandleOAuthLogin (169), so a logged-in session stays valid indefinitely if no new OAuth login starts. Cookie MaxAge (128) is client-side only. No binding to IP or user agent. Org policy: never log tokens or credentials at any level.

finding.claim: Plaintext values of password-type arguments are written to debug logs (also at line 96-99 for the shell branch). The stored audit log excludes passwords, but these debug lines do not.
finding.source: A user-submitted argument of type 'password' in a StartAction request.
finding.sink: logrus Debugf with a 'value' field containing the raw secret (protected data: credentials in logs).

trace.note: handleExecBranch calls parseActionExec for exec actions.
parseActionExec calls validateArguments.
validateArguments calls typecheckActionArgument on each declared argument, including password type.
log.WithFields({'name', 'value': values[arg.Name]}).Debugf('Arg assigned') logs the raw password.
handleShellBranch calls parseActionArguments for shell actions.
Same logging of argValue at Debug level in parseActionArguments (96-99).
TypeSafetyCheck returns nil for password (no validation), so the value passes through unchanged.
argumentTypeStorableInLog excludes password from the stored audit log, which shows the intent to keep secrets out of logs.

finding.guards_checked: Redaction (redactShellCommand arguments.go:119-137, redactExecArgs :141-147) is applied only to the command strings logged at lines 76 and 108, not to the argument-value debug lines. The leak requires the debug log level. Org policy: never log sensitive data at any log level.
